1.better: Better responses reflected wise use of the molecular structures given in the stem, thus, were able to correctly illustrate the products X and Y. Better responses reflected sound understanding of the concept of significance of sequence of amino acids in a polypeptide chain through sickle cell anaemia. Such responses validated the alteration of amino acid impede function of molecule. This validation is further supported by correct elaboration of sickle cell anaemia; which included the replacement of glutamic acid by valine resulting in alteration in shape and function of red blood cells and function.
1.weaker: Weaker responses exhibited poor understanding of the illustrations of condensation reaction. Such responses were not able to identify the groups that are involved in the bond formation. In this case, responses showed bond formation between carboxylic group and hydrogen atom. Furthermore, in some of the responses, candidates illustrated the peptide bond without mentioning the removal of water molecule; therefore such responses were not credited marks. Candidates are advised to focus on the information provided in the stimulus before drafting their responses. Weaker responses displayed candidates’ poor understanding of the concept and inability to relate the stimulus with question.  In this case, candidates drafted the answers in two ways. Firstly, such responses mentioned that replacement of amino acid B with H will not alter the function of protein and drafted the memorised description of sickle cell anaemia. Secondly, they validated the change in function of protein but could not elaborate it with the example of sickle cell anaemia.

2.better: Better responses correctly named the mechanism i.e., negative feedback mechanism/ feedback inhibition in the first part of the question. In the second part of the question, better responses exhibited candidates’ thorough understanding of the concept of negative feedback mechanism. Such responses described the action of product Z given in the stimulus i.e., binding of excess amount of product (Z) at the allosteric site of enzyme 1which results in inhibition of biochemical pathway.
2.weaker: Weaker responses displayed poor comprehension of the stimulus. In the first part of the question, such responses randomly named the mechanism such as formation of enzyme- substrate complex, mechanism of enzyme action, reversible inhibition and competitive inhibition. However, in some other responses, candidates mentioned the positive feedback mechanism. This shows candidates’ misunderstanding of negative and positive feedback mechanism. In second part of the question, weaker responses mostly described the enzyme-substrate complex formation. Furthermore, some other responses explained the mechanism of enzyme action, i.e., lowering of activation energy. Some other responses provided generalised answers such as binding of inhibitor with enzymes. For better understanding it is advised to relate this concept with the biochemical pathways given in chapter bioenergetics.

3.better: Better responses displayed clear understanding of the concept of structural orientation of the organelles present in the animal cell. In part ‘a’ of the question, such responses named the P side as forming site/ synthesis side and cis-face of Golgi apparatus. In part ‘b’ of the question, these responses provided the reason of directionality of P and Q. Such responses, drafted as, P is directed towards endoplasmic reticulum to receive transport vesicles coming from endoplasmic reticulum. Similarly, Q is directed towards plasma membrane to transport material outside of the cell.
3.weaker: Weaker responses incorrectly named the labelled side in first part of the question. Such response identified as cell wall/ lysosomes/ plasma membrane and microtubules. In second part of the question, these responses provided vague answers, such as, p is directed to endoplasmic reticulum to function properly and Q is directed towards plasma membrane to provide support and protection. Teachers are advised to unpack the meaning of ‘cis’ side of Golgi apparatus which means same side of endoplasmic reticulum. Understanding the meaning of scientific terminologies helps in better understanding of structure and function.  Furthermore, it is highly recommended to relate the position, structure and functions of different oragnelles.

4.better: Better responses wisely inferred the diagram to identify the life cycle of bacteriophage, i.e. lytic cycle in the part ‘a’ of the question. Similarly, in part ‘b’ of the question, these responses provided correct reason of their identification by mentioning lysis of the bacterial cell at the end of cycle. In part ‘c’ of the question, these responses described the stage III by highlighting the control of host’s bio-synthetic machinery by bacteriophage, likewise, in stage IV, synthesis of viral components such as DNA, proteins, head and capsid is included in their description.
4.weaker: Weaker responses incorrectly identified the life cycle of bacteriophage, therefore, provided irrelevant answers to the rest of the questions. Such responses identified the given life cycle as lysogenic in part ‘a’ of the question, therefore, failed to provide correct reason in part ‘b’ of the question. These responses mentioned ambiguous answers like attachment of bacteriophage with the host cell wall/ injection of viral DNA into host cell.  In part ‘c’ of the question, such responses provided vague description of each stage. Initiation of replication viral DNA and insertion of viral DNA into the host cell DNA in stage III and IV respectively were frequently mentioned. Hence, these responses reveal a significant confusion between lysogenic and lytic cycle of bacteriophage. Teachers are advised to provide worksheet having missing steps of each of lysogenic and lytic cycle for more practice.

5.better: Better responses correctly mentioned evidences of evolution such as presence of photosynthetic pigments chlorophyll a and b and carotenoids in plants and green algae, /presence of similar energy reserve in the form of starch/ presence of similar cell wall/ presence of photosystem I and II/and showing similar RNA sequencing. Better responses correctly described the parasexual mode of reproduction of phylum deuteromycota.  Such responses highlighted exchange of portions of chromosomes of two nuclei lying in the same hypha. Moreover, other credit worthy responses described asexual mode of reproduction through conidia and spore formation.
5.weaker: Weaker responses exhibited ambiguity in the concept of evolution of plants from green algae. These responses mentioned general features of plants and green algae. Moreover, few of the responses mentioned distinguishing characteristics of   plants and green algae.  Such as plant body is differentiated into root, stem and leaves, whereas, green algae has thallus body/ plants have vascular bundles, whereas, green algae do not possess. However, some candidates mentioned the placement of green algae in the kingdom Protista. Weaker responses revealed candidates’ poor concept of imperfect fungi i.e. deutromycota. These responses mentioned mode of reproduction as sexual and asexual. However, some responses mentioned the asexual reproduction with incorrect description i.e. budding and binary fission. Therefore these responses were unable to obtain full marks.

6.better: Better responses exhibited thorough understanding of the key terms, i.e. ‘characteristic features’,  therefore,  were able to state features such as absence of vascular bundles/ dominant gametophyte/ attachment of sporophyte to gametophyte/ homospory/, seta and capsule/ confined to damp shady places (dependant on water for reproduction)/ most of the body is parenchymatous/ amphibious in nature/ possesse psuedo stem and leaves/ plant body is gametophtye / presence of rhizoids for water absoprtion/ heteromorphic alternation of generation. Better responses manifested comprehensive understanding of the terms, i.e. inflorescene, placentation and flower symmetry.  These responses clearly differentiated the characteristics of solanacea and fabaceae by differentiating the inflorescence on the basis of arrangement of flowers on the shoot such as axillary cyme or combination of cymes/ helicoid/ axillary umbellate cyme and racemose/ solitary axillary respectively. Similarly, differentiated placentation on the basis of ovules attached to the wall of ovary such as axile and marginal placentation in solanacea and fabacea respectively. Likewise, flower symmetry is differentiated on the basis of arrangement of floral leaves, i.e. actinomorphic/ regular/ radial symmetry or weakly zygomorphic and zygomorphic/ bilateral symmetry in slonacea and fabacea respectively. Those responses which mentioned the correct floral formula were also credit marks.
6.weaker: Weaker responses showed apparent lack of understanding of the key term given in the question that led to irrelevant answers. Such responses ‘stated’ the general features rather than the ‘characteristics’ features. Majority of these responses stated multicellularity and autorophic/ photosynthetic nature as the characteristic feature. Some other responses stated the memorised features of fungi, tracheophtyes and sub-phylum of the Kingdom Plantae. Candidates are advised to identify and understand the key word(s) given in the question. Weaker responses displayed poor understanding of the terms, therefore failed to differentiate correctly. Majority of these responses differentiated on the basis of vegetative characteristics, such as, habitat, root and stem conditions of solanacea and fabaceea were given. Few responses struggled to provide the floral formula. Moreover, some responses differentiated on the basis of economic importance. However, some of the candidates swapped the differentiating points of solanacea and fabacea. Teachers are advised to integrate the related topic given in the practical and theory syllabus for better understanding. Moreover, facilitate the candidates with worksheets having explanation of each term with the diagram.

7.better: Better responses clearly described the mechanism through which electron transport chain utilises the proton gradient to produce ATP. Such responses described that NADH and FADH2 carry high energy electrons from the glycolysis and Krebs cycle to the electron transport chain. These electrons are pulled along electron transport chain they release energy that is used to pump protons across the cristae membrane, and this creates a proton gradient. This gradient is stored or potential energy. Chemiosmosis uses the potential energy in the form of proton gradient to convert ADP to ATP. For this a special complex is used called ATP synthase. During the diffusion of protons through the ATP synthase electrons are used to make ATP. Those responses which provided correct description of ATP formation through electron transport chain in photosynthesis and respiration were credited full marks.
7.weaker: Weaker responses exhibited confusion in phosphorylation and electron transport chain. Most frequently appearing weak answer was photolysis of water and use of electrons in electron transport chain. Furthermore, few responses described the reactions of Calvin cycle. Other responses provided very brief description of meaning of chemiosmosis.

8.better: Better responses correctly identified the secretory cells by naming goblet cells/ mucous secreting cells in part ‘a’ of the question. In part ‘b' of the question, better responses showed thorough understanding of the anatomy of small intestine and large intestine. These responses mentioned difference in number of divisions, length, size of lumen, presence of specialized structures for example villi and internal circular folds and overall structure of small and large intestine.
8.weaker: Weaker responses exhibited candidates’ poor understanding of nuts and bolts of comparative anatomy and histology of small and large intestine. In part ‘a’ of the question, these responses mentioned all the memorised names of secretory cells related to digestive system. For example, the frequently written names were zymogen cells/ oxyntic cells and parietal cells. In part ‘b’ of the question, majority of these responses differentiated small and large intestine on the basis their function. Such as dipeptide, maltose and fatty acids are converted into smaller subunits in small intestine whereas large intestine is not involve in digestion/ absorption of materials takes place in small intestine whereas, in large intestine reabsorption of water takes place.

9.better: Better responses displayed complete knowledge of causative agent and symptoms of tuberculosis by stating the correct name of causative agent i.e., Mycobacterium tuberculosis and   symptoms such as cough/ shortness of breath/ weight loss and septum with bleeding.
9.weaker: Weaker responses provided either incorrect or incomplete name of causative agent of tuberculosis. Furthermore, these responses stated irrelevant symptoms such as diarrhoea/ abdominal pain/ dry mouth/ patches on body and mood swings. However, some responses stated generalised symptoms like fever and weakness were awarded marks.

10a.better: Better responses in first part of the question, revealed thorough understanding of chemistry of phospholipid molecule and its structural adaptability in different conditions. These responses described the formation of micelles such that when phospholipid molecules are placed in water, the lipid ends (hydrophobic) of molecules tend to aggregate forming micelles with a phosphate group projecting out into the water. Further, these molecules form a bilayer with the polar ends facing water and non-polar ends facing each other. In second part of question, these responses obtained full marks by providing complete description of role of phospholipid in terms of protection of cell against pathogens/ transport of materials in and out of cell through different means like phagocytosis, pinocytosis, transport protein, gated channels and exocytosis/ conduction of nerve impulse in nerve cells/ regulation of cellular composition/ maintenance of cell shape and determination cell identity.
10a.weaker: Weaker responses were unable to describe the condition of phospholipid molecule when placed in water in first part of question. However, some responses described the general structure of phospholipid molecules but failed to articulate in the condition asked. Some responses drafted the chemical composition of different classes of lipid such as composition of triglycerides/ waxes/ saturated and unsaturated fatty acids. In second part of the question, revealed candidates’ limited knowledge and understanding about the functions of phospholipid membrane. Majority of these responses described semi- permeability of membrane and protection of cell only. Moreover, few responses elaborated the composition of the phospholipids. Additionally, these responses mentioned the functions of other organelles of cell such as functions of Golgi apparatus and mitochondria were frequently given. Teachers are advised to categorise functions of phospholipid membrane while teaching the topic.

10b.better: Better responses revealed sound understanding of evolution of reptiles by describing the adaptive features of reptiles such as development of copulatory organ for internal mode of fertilisation/ development of amniotic egg/ shelled egged/ presence of dry scaly skin to prevent them from dissection and limbs for efficient locomotion. Similarly, in second part of the question, these responses mentioned the features of amphibian which limit their chances of survival on land are permeable and moist skin/ external mode of fertilisation/ unprotected eggs/ eggs having insufficient amount of yolk/ lack of amnion and incomplete metamorphosis.
10b.weaker: Weaker responses provided generalised adaptive features of reptiles in the first part of the question. These responses mentioned that their circulatory/ digestive/ reproductive/ excretory and immune systems are efficient for the successful land adaptation. Furthermore, these responses identified particular examples of reptiles and described their characteristic features such as snakes reduced limb for efficient locomotion/ crocodile developed four chambered heart/ chameleon has ability to camouflage environment. Similarly, in second part of the question, these responses provided ambiguous answers such as amphibians get unsuitable environmental conditions due to which amphibians get limited chance of survival. Moreover, these responses drafted generalised answers such as amphibians are multicellular animals/ clod blooded and heterotrophs. Few responses elaborated meaning of amphibians regardless of relating it with features which impede their chances of survival on land.

11a.better: Better responses displayed sound understanding of distribution of tissues in human respiratory system by correctly identifying trachea and bronchi in the first part of the question. In second part of the question, these responses provided relevant function of tissues. Majority of the responses written the function of mucous glands, smooth muscles and ciliated epithelium. These responses highlighted the main function tissues such as contraction and relaxation of smooth muscles alter the diameter of lumen of gas exchange organs, ciliated epithelium sweep mucous containing dust particle and mucous gland humidify the passing air.  Few responses described the function of elastic fibre, as, they allow the air to be forced out of the alveoli during exhalation.
11a.weaker: Weaker responses exhibited candidates’ poor knowledge of histology of organs involved in gaseous exchange in the first part of the question. These responses randomly named the memorised name of organs such as larynx/ pharynx/ lungs and alveoli. In second part of the question revealed candidates carelessness in reading and understanding of the question. Majority of the candidates described the function of mucus glands and smooth muscles with reference to digestive system. Such responses described the function of mucus gland that their secretion (mucous) protects the stomach wall from damage by hydrochloric acid. Similarly, the function of smooth muscles is in movement of bolus in oesophagus/ churning of food in stomach. Moreover, function of ciliated epithelium and elastic fibres were incorrectly given. For example, ciliated epithelium trap dust particles and elastic fibres help in movement of lungs. These responses confuse with the spongy feature of lungs with elasticity. Candidates are highly recommended to read the question completely and carefully to avoid these blunders.

11b.better: Better responses displayed wise use of diagrams in describing each phase in the first part of the question. Moreover, these responses met the demand of the question by focusing on the blood pressure change in their description. These responses related relaxed condition of atria and ventricle with lower blood pressure. Similarly, in phase II is blood pressure in the atria exceeds than ventricles as the contraction of the atrial walls forces the blood into the ventricles. In phase III, ventricles contract and increased blood within the ventricles forcing atrio-ventricular valves to close and preventing backflow of blood into atria. With the atrio- ventricular valves closed the pressure in ventricles rises. In second part of the question, better responses clearly described the role of sino-atrial node and atrio-ventricular node in the regulation of cardiac cycle. Furthermore, these responses mentioned the role of Purkinjees fibres and bundle of hiss in their description.
11b.weaker: Weaker responses exhibited poor understanding of diagrammatic presentation of phases of heart in first part of the question. Moreover, these responses were unable to relate the condition of heart chambers with blood pressure change. These responses drafted description of structure of heart and its function. Such as heart consist of four chambers/ right atria and left atria collect deoxygenated and oxygenated blood respectively/ right atria and right ventricle are separated by tricuspid valve/ left atria and left ventricle are separated by bicuspid valve/ pulmonary artery emerge from right ventricle and pulmonary vein emerge from left ventricle and semilunar valves are present in pulmonary trunk. Few other responses provided incomplete description by only mentioning the contraction and relaxation of heart chamber each phase without refereeing the blood pressure change. These responses were not warded full marks. In second part of question, these responses either provided incomplete or incorrect answers. Such as Thand  the  responses described some steps of anaerobic respiration, electron transport chain, photosynthesis, Calvin cycle etc. Teachers are highly recommended to teach these concepts describing the mission of each process or step; this will enable students to differentiate among different concepts in bioenergetics.
